reviewer: Performance B — timing, weight and emotional clarity

perClaimDecisions.claim: PB1: held-peek inference versus temporal joke
perClaimDecisions.decision: Accept A’s distinction; retain the narrow static concern.
perClaimDecisions.reason: My observation concerns the labelled 1550-ms thumbnail, not recognition of the full joke. The authored conceal/reveal/reconceal sequence can communicate mischief even if an isolated peek reads ambiguously. The selected static fallback still deserves its own inspection because its users do not receive that sequence.
perClaimDecisions.acceptedWording: The full mischievous beat and its selected static fallback require separate evaluation. Thumbnail ambiguity does not establish failure of the temporal joke or require a stronger pose.

perClaimDecisions.claim: PB2: pre-contact compression versus failed cushioning
perClaimDecisions.decision: Accept the evidence limit and refine my wording.
perClaimDecisions.reason: The sampled headY values establish downward head movement relative to the body before contact, with maximum compression at 1060 ms. Calling that movement cushioning assigns a function the samples cannot prove. Neither source nor supplied frames establish a failed landing. Coordinated anticipatory movement may be appropriate.
perClaimDecisions.acceptedWording: Head compression develops before contact and peaks at contact; its contribution to perceived weight remains a normal-speed playback question. No later compression or recovery is mandatory.

perClaimDecisions.decision: Accept; total duration is descriptive, not a useful quality proxy.
perClaimDecisions.reason: The 2500–4100-ms range combines active response, secondary accents, recovery and holds. Thinking’s late toe tap and Surprise’s early lift already show different structures. Smoothstep endpoint stops are a reason to inspect the flow of specific connected actions, not proof that whole clips feel alike.
perClaimDecisions.acceptedWording: Compare first readable response, reveal timing, accent spacing and settlement in normal-speed playback. Do not shorten or equalize complete clips merely because their runtimes overlap.

perClaimDecisions.claim: A’s PA1–PA4 and shared preservation principles
perClaimDecisions.reason: Intention changes, dominant hand actions, the corrected continuous descent and broad-affect evidence are supported by the materials I inspected. Tiny anatomy, theme parity, silence, finite endings and restrained wings remain valid. This agreement does not extend to unseen playback or human interpretation.

perClaimDecisions.decision: Agree to show and describe the baseline first; object to making baseline failure a prerequisite for reversible exploration.
perClaimDecisions.reason: A one-variable alternative can reveal a useful expressive choice even when the baseline works. A demonstrated named benefit is necessary to adopt a change; a preexisting defect is not necessary to author and compare it. This matches root’s forthcoming team scope.

acceptedWording: Agreement concerns a bounded performance experiment plan, not final-art approval or an automatic nine score.

Inspect the baseline first. Permit narrowly scoped, reversible timing alternatives for a named expressive question. Adopt an alternative only when comparison identifies a named benefit without violating anatomy, theme parity or continuity; otherwise retain the baseline.
Observe current Curious beside a real content cue to test attention and thought change; this need not introduce scenery.

requestedChanges.requirement: Replace “For a demonstrated failing beat only” with “For a named expressive question or demonstrated difficulty”. Keep the one-variable and retain-baseline conditions.
Replace “only if playback identifies weight loss” with “as a reversible comparison for a named contact/recovery question; adoption requires a named benefit”. Baseline observation remains first.
Keep the lack of playback and human evidence as named limits. Clarify that hypothetical failure does not justify wholesale retiming, while bounded exploration remains permitted.

substantiveObjections: The unchanged proposal forbids alternatives unless a failing beat is demonstrated. I object to that unnecessary exploration gate, not to the preservation rules, baseline inspection, or benefit requirement for adoption.

unchangedProposalScope.explanation: I endorse the stated experiment-plan scope. I cannot endorse the unchanged operative wording until the failure-only prerequisite is removed.

limits: No new artwork or playback was reviewed during deliberation. The independent null score remains unchanged. This response approves no production modification and claims no audience result.
